full_judgment: 17. The learned Attorney-General has questioned the very maintainability of the suit of the plaintiffs and referred the decision reported in 43 DLR (AD) 225 as noticed above. Now with regard to the maintainability of the suit, I am of the view that the above cited decision is not applicable in the facts that in the above cited case the plaintiff filed the suit for permanent injunction for restraining the defendants from entering into CS plot Nos. 784 and 802 appertaining to CS khatian No. 125 of mouza Galtoir PS Chirirbandar District Dinajpur. The trial Court upon consideration of materials on record found that Dinomoni inherited the land of CS khatian No. 125 from her husband and that her son-in-law Janaki looked after her properties and there was no basis of noting of the alleged exchange in the CS khatian, the trial Court held that Janaki got his son Lalit''s name included in the CS khatian fraudulently, that Dinomoni had title in all the lands including plot No. 784 and that the presumption of correctness of the record of right was rebutted. The trial Court further found that in the kabala dated 18-1-1938 executed by Dinomoni in favour of Janaki, there was a reference to two other plots besides the two suit plots: that Janaki asserted his title and possession in the suit lands and executed Ext.1 the kabala dated 1-4-1957 in favour of the plaintiff who after purchase got his name mutated and got rent receipts. The trial Court also accepted the evidence of PWs 2 and 3 in support of the plaintiffs'' case and rejected the evidence of the defendants'' witneses. The appellate Court upheld the trial Courts, decree with regard to plot No. 802 but dismissed the plaintiffs'' prayer with regard to the other plot namely, the plot No. 784 after finding that the plaintiff failed to prove his prima facie title and exclusive possession there. In the above cited case the plaintiff assailed the presumption of CS khatian but in the instant case the plaintiffs have not assailed the presumption of khatian as the SA and RS khatians already stood in the name of the plaintiffs. Furthermore, the plaintiffs in the instant case proved this prima facie case and both the courts below having considered the materials on record found exclusive possession of the plaintiffs in disputed plots.
